We All Belong
Reception 2027 Cohort - Open Days
Reception open day tours will be held every Monday starting from Monday 21st September at 5pm.
Attendance Mascots
Quanley and Curious Quinn are here to champion attendance at North Beckton Primary School. They will be here to support our children to achieve, build friendships and enjoy school. Support us in promoting our new attendance mascots.
The Tapscott Learning Trust
We are delighted to present a short film about our schools and the experiences of our children, parents and staff. Our schools may have spaces. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XaWCHz89kH4
Starting School
We currently have spaces at North Beckton Primary. For admission information, please click here.
If you would like to apply for a school place please fill out an In-Year Application form. To access the form, click here.
Starting Reception - How can I help my child get ready?
To find out more information please click here.

Headteacher's Welcome
It is my pleasure to welcome you to North Beckton Primary and Nursery School – the school where “We All Belong” and I hope that you enjoy your visit to our website. Our school has continued to go from strength to strength, ensuring that we are committed to developing the whole child in partnership with parents and carers, through our exciting curriculum.
Our curriculum is rich in providing the necessary academic skills and knowledge, equipping the children for their life beyond North Beckton. Our curriculum has been designed to reflect and celebrate the diverse and inclusive community that we are.
North Beckton Primary School became part of The Tapscott Learning Trust in 2019. This is a trust based on partnership, ensuring the best possible quality education for our children and meeting the needs of our local community.
Please explore our website as it has lots of information about all the amazing things that we do here. If we can be of any further help, please do not hesitate to make direct contact with the school. Our office staff will give you a warm welcome, and will offer a wealth of information.
“Go North Beckton Go!”
Shella Lawrenson - Executive Head Teacher Bal Kettory - Head of School

pageCache.text:
Residential Trips
Fairplay House – November 2025
Year 5 and 6 Trip to Fairplay House: An Unforgettable Adventure
Day 1: The children have arrived safely at Fairplay house – the children have been unpacking their bags and setting up their rooms. They are about to have a lesson in making their beds, before heading out to their first activities!
After enjoying a delicious and nutritious lunch, the children completed their first activity of the day with great enthusiasm. Working together as a team, they then prepared their own beds and showed fantastic cooperation. The children are now warming up by having dinner and listening to the briefing for the night walk.
Enjoying a hot chocolate whilst watching a story, Pyjamas on and ready for bed!
Day 2: The children had a well rested night’s sleep and awoke to a beautiful sunny morning, albeit rather chilly! They had a delicious breakfast which included a selection of fruits, croissants, cereals and juices. After breakfast, they had their room inspections, with the winning groups being announced before the morning brief with the instructors. Children have wrapped up warm and have left for their morning activities.
Children enjoyed an amazing morning completing their activities. After that, they recharged their batteries with a delicious lunch of tomato soup and croutons, sandwiches, fruit, crisps and chocolate cookies! They have been brilliant and overcome many fears. The teamwork and bonds they have built have developed and deepened through encouragement and support of one another.
Day 3: Tired eyes for the morning briefing this morning. All ready and full of optimism for the last activity. Suitcases packed and ready for the coach later today.
The activities included:
Caving: The children ventured and explored the caves. The children faced the challenge of navigating enclosed spaces, learning to remain calm and trust both their abilities and the support of their peers.
High Rope: The high ropes and G3 swing tested the children's courage with heights, created resilience and facing their fears and also supporting their peers.
G3 Swing: The high ropes and G3 swing tested the children's courage with heights, created resilience and facing their fears and also supporting their peers.
Everyone has had an amazing time making wonderful memories and creating stronger bonds than before. Well done to them all!

pageCache.pageTitle: North Beckton Primary School - What We Are Learning
pageCache.text:
What We Are Learning
Nursery Learning
Autumn Term
Autumn Fun at Forest Schools! This Autumn, our nursery children had so much fun during our visit to Forest School! We went on a little adventure to collect colourful leaves, pine cones, and conkers. The children loved feeling all the different textures and using the leaves to make bright, beautiful prints. Back in nursery, we made a lovely display to show off our amazing artwork! It was messy, creative, and full of smiles. Take a peek at our display and enjoy the magic of Autumn with us!
Autumn Term 2
We started our exciting new cooking activities in the Nursery! We absolutely loved baking our very own fig cupcakes. We picked fresh figs from the tree in our nursery garden, then chopped them up and mixed them with all the ingredients. The cupcakes came out delicious, and we had so much fun making them together!
Spring Term
Our Nursery Easter Bonnet Parade was a burst of colour and creativity! The children proudly wore their handmade bonnets decorated with flowers, chicks, and bunnies, parading around with big smiles for friends. It was a joyful celebration of spring, filled with laughter, applause and plenty of Easter cheer.
Summer Term
Early Years Bug Ball: Our Early Years children had a wonderful time at Forest School for our Bug Ball! Everyone dressed up as their favourite creepy-crawlies and had lots of fun in forest schools. We gathered around a warm campfire to sing fun songs and danced like little bugs through the trees. The day finished with a brilliant costume parade which the children thoroughly enjoyed.
Reception Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026-27
Autumn Term
We Begin Our Journey in Reception! During the first weeks in Reception, we spent time getting to know each other, what we like, what we are good at and what makes us special. We are very proud of each and every child, parents and carers who played a vital part in ensuring a smooth and successful transition into new routines.
Autumn Term 2
Back to school began with something truly special, tactile Story Time led by our amazing school librarian! Children immersed themselves in The Very Hungry Caterpillar story through touch and imagination, making it a joyful and memorable start to the new term.
Children In Need: Thank you so much for your incredible support and generosity on Pudsey Day! Your contributions, from the wonderful dressing up to the kind donations, have truly made a difference.
The children had a fantastic time participating in all the activities and learning about the importance of helping others. Your support not only helped us raise valuable funds for Children in Need but also created a memorable and meaningful experience for everyone.
We truly appreciate your continued partnership as parents and carers in making these events so special for everyone.
Spring Term
Reading Together: It was lovely to see so many parents and carers join us for our Reading Morning. Our classrooms were full of smiles as families snuggled up to share stories and flip through colourful books together. Seeing the children so excited to read with their grown-ups made the morning feel really special. Thank you to the parents and carers for coming along and helping us make reading such a fun part of our school day!
Biscuits, Flames and Big Smiles at Forest School
Our first Forest School campfire was unforgettable! We gathered around the warm, crackling flames, feeling both excited and a little amazed as the sparks drifted into the air. Everyone took turns toasting marshmallows, watching them slowly turn golden before we could enjoy the perfect gooey treat. We laughed, sang our favourite songs and enjoyed being together outdoors. The magical moment was calm, fun and full of good energy, leaving everyone feeling cheerful, connected and belonging.
Spring Term 2
Our Reception Easter Bonnet Parade was a burst of colour and creativity! The children proudly wore their handmade bonnets decorated with flowers, chicks, and bunnies, parading around with big smiles for friends. It was a joyful celebration of spring, filled with laughter, applause and plenty of Easter cheer.
Summer Term
Early Years Bug Ball: Our Early Years children had a wonderful time at Forest School for our Bug Ball! Everyone dressed up as their favourite creepy-crawlies and had lots of fun in forest schools. We gathered around a warm campfire to sing fun songs and danced like little bugs through the trees. The day finished with a brilliant costume parade which the children thoroughly enjoyed.
Year 1 Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026–27
Autumn Term
Class Trip: As part of our Place of Worship topic, we visited St Mary Magdalene’s Church in East Ham. We were welcomed by Reverend Katherine, who told us all about the church’s fascinating history. Did you know it’s over 900 years old?
We had a wonderful time drawing and counting the crosses, learning about Christian symbols, and even watching Reverend Katherine baptise our baby doll, Sarah! To end our visit, we were treated to a special moment; Reverend Katherine playing the church organ for us.
It was a truly memorable and inspiring morning!
Autumn Term 2
Year 1 were taken on a magical multisensory Christmas journey to recall the story of Jesus' birth. We met different characters from the story, such as the Angel Gabriel, we smelt frankincense and myrrh, dressed up as shepherds and wise men and even tasted some bread made by Mary!
Class Trip: Year 1 enjoyed an exciting school trip to the Young V&A in Bethnal Green as part of our history topic on old and new toys. The children explored fascinating displays of toys from the past and compared them with the toys we play with today. They asked thoughtful questions, took part in hands-on activities, and had lots of fun learning how toys have changed over time. It was a memorable day that brought our historical learning to life!
Spring Term
Art Lesson: As part of our art learning, we explored the work of the famous artist Yayoi Kusama. We discovered that she is known for using lots of dots in her artwork and that she loves creating art inspired by fruit.
We had great fun using clay to sculpt our own fruits before carefully painting them in Yayoi Kusama’s style, using bright colours and patterns of dots. The finished pieces look fantastic, and we are very proud of our creative work!
Summer Term
Year 1 - West Ham Park Trip: This week, Year 1 had a fantastic time on our school trip to West Ham Park. In a hands-on Stone Age shelter building workshop, the children became prehistoric builders and learnt how to make shelters using different shaped sticks found around them.
After testing their survival skills, our young historians turned into eco-artists. Using natural materials found around the park, they crafted unique natural book marks and sculpted brilliant characters out of clay. It was a lovely, sun-filled day of creativity and outdoor learning!
Year 2 Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026–27
Autumn Term
Outdoor Learning: The children had a wonderful time exploring the forest school as part of their learning about minibeasts in Science. They carefully looked under logs, leaves, and stones to discover where minibeasts like to live, and also searched up high in the trees to spot different habitats. It was an exciting hands-on experience that helped the children understand how living things make their homes in the natural environment.
Autumn Term 2:
Class Trip: Year 2 had a fantastic time exploring the Tower of London as part of their history learning. The children enjoyed discovering the Crown Jewels, learning about their importance and sparkle, and exploring the Tudor houses to find out how people lived in the past. A highlight of the visit was meeting the famous ravens and hearing why they are so important to the Tower. It was an exciting and memorable way to bring history to life.
Spring Term
Summer Term
Our Year 2 students had an absolute blast at our recent movie night! The fun kicked off with everyone settling in to enjoy a delicious spread of sandwiches and tasty snacks with their friends. Once the treats were finished, it was time for the main event. The children cozied up for a fantastic double-feature, laughing along with the hilarious underwater adventures in The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, followed by the epic, music-filled journey of Moana 2. It was a magical evening filled with big smiles, great cinema, and wonderful company.
Year 3 Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026–27
Autumn Term
Topic: This term, Year 3 have been exploring the fascinating world of Ancient Egypt. We’ve learnt all about mummification, pharaohs, and the River Nile, discovering what life was like thousands of years ago. One of our favourite activities was role-playing as Howard Carter, uncovering a hidden tomb filled with treasures — including a mummy and canopic jars! We even had great fun practising the mummification process on each other!
Science: This term in Science, Year 3 have been learning all about forces and magnets. We’ve enjoyed carrying out exciting investigations to explore how these forces work. We tested how friction changes on different surfaces and experimented with magnets to answer our own scientific questions. It’s been a fun and hands-on way to discover how forces affect the world around us!
Autumn Term 2
Year 3 had a thrilling adventure at the British Museum this week! The children were amazed to see Cleopatra’s mummy, a real-life glimpse into Ancient Egypt. They also explored the Sutton Hoo treasures, uncovered the secrets of the Rosetta Stone, and discovered fascinating Viking and Egyptian artefacts. It was a day full of wonder, curiosity, and history coming alive!
Starry Night: Year 3 had an absolutely magical Starry Night event, staying at school until 6pm for an evening filled with excitement and wonder. The fun began with cosy movie time and snacks, before everyone headed outside for stargazing under the beautiful night sky. Pupils listened to an inspiring story about a brave star, then showed bravery of their own by putting on an amazing talent show filled with laughter and confidence. The adventure continued with a thrilling night walk around the school, followed by the delicious treat of toasting marshmallows, making gooey s’mores, and sipping warm hot chocolate. It truly was a magical, unforgettable night for Year 3!
Spring Term
Spring Term 2
Class Trip: Year 3 had a fantastic visit to the London Docklands Museum today, where they enjoyed an exciting and educational day exploring the past. The children were fully engaged as they discovered the rich history of the Royal Docks, learning how they played a vital role in London’s growth as a centre for trade and industry. Through interactive exhibits and fascinating displays, the pupils gained a deeper understanding of how goods from around the world once passed through the docks. It was a fun and memorable experience for everyone, and the children returned to school inspired and full of new knowledge.
Pupil Voice: I like when we went to Sailor town because we could experience what London looked like in those days. Sofia
Pupil Voice: We got to smell different spices like cloves, tea and coffee. Sami
Pupil Voice: My favourite part was the party sounds I could hear in sailor town. Matteo
Summer Term
Class Trip: South West Reform Synagogue Visit
Year 3 visited the South West Reform Synagogue in Newbury Park for an enriching learning experience. The children learnt all about Judaism, explored the key features of a synagogue, and had the opportunity to see the Torahs up close. They also examined a range of religious artefacts and enjoyed tasting traditional challah bread. It was a memorable and insightful visit that deepened their understanding of Jewish faith and culture.
Year 4 Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026–27
Autumn Term
Spring Term
Class Trip: Year 4 had an explosive day of learning on their recent trip to the Natural History Museum! As part of our topic on volcanoes and earthquakes, the children explored fascinating exhibits and discovered how powerful forces beneath the Earth shape our planet. The highlight of the visit was an exciting hands-on workshop, where pupils learnt about how volcanoes erupt and why earthquakes happen. The students asked brilliant questions, shared their knowledge, and left feeling like real geologists. It was a fantastic day full of curiosity, discovery, and a few rumbling surprises!
Pupil Voice: "The school trip was brilliant because there was so much to see. I loved going into the earthquake simulator because it felt just like a real earthquake! My favourite bit was the workshop where I saw mini-volcanoes explode, and it was great fun watching my friends have a go at volunteeri
Summer Term
Year 4 Trip: Our Year 4 pupils swapped the classroom for the grand galleries of the National Portrait Gallery in London. The children had a fantastic time exploring history through art, coming face-to-face with famous figures from the past and present.
From sketching their own portraits to uncovering the stories behind the paintings, it was an incredibly inspiring day.
Have a look at our gallery to see our young historians and artists in action!
Year 5 Learning
Welcome Meeting 2026–27
Autumn Term
Maths: In the autumn term, Year 5 students have explored a variety of complex concepts that enhance their number sense and computational skills. One of the key areas of focus has been the exploration of Roman numerals, extending their understanding up to 1,000.
Pushing the boundaries of their numerical prowess, children have been mastering numbers up to 1,000,000, learning to read and write these large figures with confidence. They have delved into powers of ten and practised determining amounts that are 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000 more or less than given numbers.
Students have also developed their skills in partitioning numbers and have engaged in comparing and ordering values, which has fostered a deeper understanding of place value.
